pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/core/src/types.rs:436 ExecutionConfig is the per-execution record "persisted alongside results for post-mortem debugging". It stores tool-roster bytes, whether workspace instructions were injected, and the continuation mode, but it has no digest or size of the assembled prompt. A repo-wide grep for prompt_digest, prompt_bytes and prompt_size in the Rust sources found nothing, so 'what was this run told?' cannot be answered from artifacts (the unrecorded-send failure).

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/core/src/types.rs:436 The persisted execution snapshot has no fingerprint, version stamp, digest or size field for the prompt it fed; only booleans and counts for some layers (has_workspace_instructions, tool_roster_bytes).

src-tauri/core/src/types.rs:352 The regime in which the CLI holds the conversation is a typed variant of its own (CLI --resume), separate from the client-side PromptHint continuation, so callers have to choose an ownership regime explicitly.

pairs.evidence: src/features/teams/sub_factory/AddKpiModal.tsx:45 The operator-entered project name is spliced into a hand-written task string at the call site, and useAskAthena then tags the whole string as app-composed (source 'Add KPI'). The variable's trust class is therefore decided by the call site, not declared on the variable, which is the failure variable-interpolation names.

src/features/teams/sub_factory/useAddKpi.ts:120 The AI KPI proposal passes typed fields (name, category, direction, measureKind, ...) to the backend assembler instead of pre-rendered prompt text.
